bc_twin_towers.blurb: Twin Towers is a tall wall in the Comox Lake climbing zone on Vancouver Island, near Cumberland. It has six sport routes, all bolted, spread from 5.10 up through the 5.11s to a single 5.12 line, so it suits climbers who already lead the low double digits and want something steeper. The right-hand side of the towers is the more overhanging part. The approach follows a trail that starts at the top of Carpet Rock and keeps left. Climbs here are a step up from the easier lines found on the nearby lakeside walls, and the surrounding forest keeps temperatures moderate.

bc_huckleberry_hill.blurb: Huckleberry Hill is a low-angle slab zone above the campground at Comox Lake, near Cumberland on Vancouver Island. It holds six routes: five sport and one trad, with grades running from 5.3 and 5.5 through the 5.6s to 5.8, and one 5.10a at the top end. Every climb starts from a single wide ledge that runs across the whole slab, which makes it a reasonable place for newer leaders and for beginner multi-pitch practice. The trail in passes below the Main Wall and Waterfall before cutting up to that ledge.

bc_stray_cat_alley.blurb: Stray Cat Alley is a newer sector in the creek canyon at Cypress Falls Park, West Vancouver. It has six sport routes, with one at 5.9, four in the 5.11 range and one 5.12, so the grades lean toward intermediate and strong leaders rather than beginners. The canyon stays cool through hot summer days, though the walls take a week or more to dry after heavy rain, which makes mid to late summer the usual window. The sector sits across the creek from Cougar Crag, which is the other main sport wall in the park.

bc_lower_cat_wall.blurb: Lower Cat Wall is the first of the two Cat Walls reached from the road near Castlegar, in the Arrow Lake part of the West Kootenay. It is a small crag with six routes, five sport and one trad, graded from 5.8 to 5.10a, so it works for newer leaders and anyone warming up. The Cat Walls face the sun and have lake views, and spring is the time climbers favour. Upper Cat Wall, with more routes, is a short walk further along the trail.
bc_lower_cat_wall.parking_note: Leave the car at the roadside pullout and cross the road to the start of the cut trail.
bc_lower_cat_wall.approach: A cut trail leads through forest past a large boulder; Lower Cat Wall is the first wall you reach.
